This hatred only grows worse as the game goes on, with Cloud learning more about his past and Sephiroth committing more evil deeds, most infamously his murder of Aerith Gainsborough.

This grows to massive stakes as Sephiroth attempts to bring about the end of the world in the climax of Final Fantasy VII, with Cloud and his allies fighting to stop him once and for all. While the rivalry itself is relatively muted in the original game, it has been massively explored and delved into more in spinoffs and especially the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy.

blocks.c: Ken and Ryu giving each other a fist bump before a match in 'Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike'

blocks.x: Fighting games as a genre lend themselves to rivalries more than any other genre, as even outside of the game's world, facing off against another player inherently creates a rivalry between the two players, whether it be seriously competitive or easygoing fun. In the world of fighting games, no singular rivalry symbolizes this inherent strength, like Ryu and Ken from Street Fighter, two best friends who trained under the same master to be the greatest fighters in the world.

Ryu and Ken's rivalry does not come from a place of hatred, but instead from constant friendship and respect for one another as they fight their hardest against one another to bring out the best in each other. It's a beautiful rivalry that cuts to the heart of fighting games as a genre and has only grown more prominent with each additional entry. More impactful is that Ryu and Ken have the same gameplay archetype, sharing special moves but having enough distinguishing differences to set them apart.

In terms of the iconic status of a video game rivalry, it's difficult for anything to compete with the most iconic video game character of all time facing off against the most iconic video game villain of all time. While Bowser wasn't the first villain to cross Mario's path, since Mario's origins trace back to the arcades with Donkey Kong, it cannot be denied that the constant battles against the king of koopas and this plucky plumber have made their rivalry legendary.

It's a rivalry that has been explored in many different ways across the over 100 different Mario games, although often it takes the form of Bowser being a vengeful final boss responsible for Mario's journey in the first place. Even in games where Bowser isn't the main villain, his presence and hatred of Mario are always known and apparent. It simply isn't a Mario game without Bowser, and Bowser wouldn't be nearly as impactful a villain without his exceptional contrast with Mario.

This grows to massive stakes as Sephiroth attempts to bring about the end of the world in the climax of Final Fantasy VII, with Cloud and his allies fighting to stop him once and for all. While the rivalry itself is relatively muted in the original game, it has been massively explored and delved into more in spinoffs and especially the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy.

2
Ryu and Ken

'Street Fighter' Games (1987–Present)

Fighting games as a genre lend themselves to rivalries more than any other genre, as even outside of the game's world, facing off against another player inherently creates a rivalry between the two players, whether it be seriously competitive or easygoing fun. In the world of fighting games, no singular rivalry symbolizes this inherent strength, like Ryu and Ken from Street Fighter, two best friends who trained under the same master to be the greatest fighters in the world.

Ryu and Ken's rivalry does not come from a place of hatred, but instead from constant friendship and respect for one another as they fight their hardest against one another to bring out the best in each other. It's a beautiful rivalry that cuts to the heart of fighting games as a genre and has only grown more prominent with each additional entry. More impactful is that Ryu and Ken have the same gameplay archetype, sharing special moves but having enough distinguishing differences to set them apart.

1
Mario and Bowser

'Super Mario' Games (1985–Present)

Image via Nintendo

In terms of the iconic status of a video game rivalry, it's difficult for anything to compete with the most iconic video game character of all time facing off against the most iconic video game villain of all time. While Bowser wasn't the first villain to cross Mario's path, since Mario's origins trace back to the arcades with Donkey Kong, it cannot be denied that the constant battles against the king of koopas and this plucky plumber have made their rivalry legendary.

It's a rivalry that has been explored in many different ways across the over 100 different Mario games, although often it takes the form of Bowser being a vengeful final boss responsible for Mario's journey in the first place. Even in games where Bowser isn't the main villain, his presence and hatred of Mario are always known and apparent. It simply isn't a Mario game without Bowser, and Bowser wouldn't be nearly as impactful a villain without his exceptional contrast with Mario.
